forecast-period.text: A cold front will move across SA on Tuesday. A high pressure ridge will move across the north of the state on Wednesday and Thursday and another cold front will slip across the southeast of SA early Thursday. The ridge will move eastwards early Friday then another trough will move over SA during the day followed by a cold front early Saturday. Another high pressure ridge will move across during Sunday ahead of a low pressure system expected to develop in the far west later in the day.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Morning fog patches about the ranges. Isolated showers about the agricultural areas and the far south of the pastoral districts. Maximum temperatures below average in the south but above average in the north. Fresh and gusty northwesterly winds in the far northeast. West to southwesterly winds elsewhere, but southwest to southeasterly in the northwest, tending northwesterly about the agricultural areas during the afternoon and evening.

Showers about the agricultural areas, extending over the far south of the pastoral districts during the evening. Chance of a thunderstorm about southern coastal districts. Fresh and gusty northwesterly winds ahead of a south to southwesterly change extending across the west and south.

Isolated showers about the agricultural areas, more frequent about the southern agricultural areas during the morning and early afternoon. Patchy rain developing in the southwest, west of about Ceduna, in the evening and the chance of a thunderstorm in the far southwest. Maximum temperatures above average in the north and west but below average elsewhere. Northwest to southwesterly winds about the agricultural areas, tending southeast to northeasterly further north.

text.p: Areas of rain in the west extending over the agricultural areas and the south of the pastoral districts, easing to isolated showers from the west during the afternoon and evening. Chance of a thunderstorm in the west and south. Maximum temperatures above average in the north and west but below average elsewhere. Northeast to northwesterly winds freshening ahead of a southwesterly change in the west later.

Showers about the south of the pastoral districts contracting east and clearing during the morning. Further south, showers about the southern agricultural areas becoming isolated during the afternoon then mostly clearing by evening. Chance of a morning thunderstorm about the Lower South East and Flinders districts and the south of the North East Pastoral. Maximum temperatures above average in the far northeast but below average elsewhere. Fresh to strong and gusty winds about the agricultural areas turning west to southwesterly during the morning. Southwest to southeasterly winds extending over remaining areas.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Saturday: 2 to 5 mm over the south of the pastoral districts, although local falls of 5 to 15 mm are possible in the far south. 5 to 10 mm is expected about the northern agricultural areas and 10 to 15 mm about the southern agricultural areas. Local falls of 15 to 25 mm are possible about the Mount Lofty Ranges and Lower South East. Isolated higher falls are possible about the Mount Lofty Ranges.
